opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
At our baptism, we were being prepared to receive the gifts of the Holy Spirit—though already called, as it is written in Acts of the Apostles:

“Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is made to you and to your children and to all those far off, whomever the Lord our God will call.”

Be thankful. Be grateful to Christ that you were called by name. Now you know His voice.

As it is written in the Gospel of John, “When He has driven out all His own, He walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow Him because they recognize His voice.” And in the First Epistle of Peter, “By His wounds you have been healed. For you had gone astray like sheep, but you have now returned to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.”

Be thankful.

Some say, “You had no choice—you were baptized as a baby.” But what they fail to understand is this: the promise was never bound by age or by moment. It was spoken long before—“to you and to your children and to all those far off.” I was already within that promise.

In that moment, my soul was sanctified by His grace—infused, claimed, set apart.

Now comes the response:

To live fully as a child of God, a member of His Church—not passively, but intentionally—so as to obtain, hereafter, the inheritance of Heaven.

This is not the end of something.
It is the beginning of everything.
